q: The complexity function p(n) of a minimal subshift counts the number of distinct words of length n. Morse-Hedlund theorem characterises periodic sequences by:
opts: p(n) ≤ n for all n implies the sequence is eventually periodic; p(n) < n+1 for some n implies periodic
p(n) is eventually constant iff the sequence is eventually periodic
p(n) ≥ n+1 for all n iff the sequence is not periodic
exp: Morse-Hedlund theorem: a sequence x ∈ A^ℤ is periodic iff p(n) ≤ n for some n (since p(n) ≤ n implies p(n) is eventually constant). Equivalently, x is not periodic iff p(n) ≥ n+1 for all n. The minimal complexity for non-periodic sequences is the Sturmian case p(n) = n+1.
